devils.title: The Devils
devils.text: Russell’s church-and-state nightmare is a defining work of transgressive cinema, not merely a Halloween curiosity. Choose the restored print this week: IFC and FLC have 35mm, while BAM’s engagement is digital.

zven.title: Zvenygora / Звенигора
zven.text: A thousand years of Ukrainian legend collapse into Dovzhenko’s radical montage. The archive print and new live score make this the week’s most irreplaceable repertory event.
zven.event: Live score by medukha: Asia Mieleszko, Max Temnogorod and Salina Kuo

amoeba.title: Amoeba
amoeba.text: Four misfits in an elite Singapore girls’ school invent a gang against the country’s machinery of conformity. The combination of Southeast Asian discovery and a first local filmmaker conversation earns priority over familiar repertory.
amoeba.event: Q&A with Siyou Tan, moderated by Cristine Brache

nostos.title: Nostos: The Return
nostos.text: Piavoli retells the Odyssey through landscape, sound and half-understood language. For your Apichatpong and formally adventurous tastes, this nearly wordless experience is a stronger discovery than another prestige release.

harlem.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
harlem.venue: Film at Lincoln Center; Film Forum
harlem.when: FLC Sat Oct 17 · 6:00 & 6:30 PM; Sun Oct 18 · 3:30 & 4:00 PM. Film Forum Fri Oct 16 · 6:00 & 7:00 PM
harlem.text: William Greaves’s extraordinary gathering of Harlem Renaissance elders finally becomes a feature through his son’s work. Choose a guest-bearing show rather than treating this as an interchangeable documentary run.
harlem.event: FLC: David Greaves, Liani Greaves & Anne de Mare. Film Forum: David & Liani Greaves.

east.title: From the East / D’est
east.text: Akerman’s tracking shots and patient queues make post-Soviet transition palpable without explanatory dialogue. This is an especially good extension of your interest in duration and minimalism after Hong and Hamaguchi.

home.title: No Home Movie
home.text: Akerman’s last feature finds immense pressure inside conversations with her mother and empty domestic space. It is a demanding, intimate companion to D’est rather than a conventional biographical documentary.

insider.title: The Insider
insider.text: Mann makes institutional pressure visible through bodies, architecture and electronic atmosphere. The real reporter at the center of the story appearing with Pablo Torre is the substantive upgrade over a regular revival.
insider.event: Q&A with Lowell Bergman & Pablo Torre

president.title: All the President’s Men
president.text: Pakula’s procedural remains a masterpiece of rooms, voices and uncertain evidence. Carl Bernstein’s conversation makes this more than a timely canonical rewatch.
president.event: Carl Bernstein & Maggie Haberman; moderator Natalie Kitroeff

paris.title: Paris Was a Woman
paris.when: Fri Oct 16 · 6:40 PM; Sat Oct 17 · 2:30 PM; Sun Oct 18 · 6:45 PM; Mon Oct 19 · 8:00 PM; Wed Oct 21 · 6:00 PM
paris.text: Schiller and Andrea Weiss reconstruct a network of women artists beyond the usual masculine mythology of interwar Paris. The restoration’s first weekend is unusually rich in filmmaker and author access.
paris.event: Fri Q&A Schiller & Weiss, moderator Laura Flanders + signing; Sat same guests, moderator Jane Gaines; Sun intro Kirsten Larvick, Schiller & Weiss

highlow.title: High and Low / 天国と地獄
highlow.text: Kurosawa turns a ransom demand into an exact map of class and moral obligation. It deserves a visible canonical slot, but conflicts with the rarer Nostos screening; choose Piavoli if you already know this well.

oldboy.title: Oldboy / 올드보이
oldboy.text: Park’s formal control and corrosive revenge structure make this influential cult cinema rather than a generic late show. It is a strong theatrical option, though less scarce than the day’s live-score and reporter events.

okja.title: Okja / 옥자
okja.when: Fri Oct 16 · 1:45 PM; Sat Oct 17 · noon
okja.text: Bong’s tonal collisions turn a creature adventure into a critique of industrial consumption. The theatrical return is welcome, although Saturday directly conflicts with Zvenygora and should rank below it.

redline.title: Redline
redline.text: Koike’s deliriously drawn racing spectacle deserves a screen big enough to make its labor and velocity visible. This is the midnight pick for sheer formal excess rather than another familiar horror repeat.

great.title: The Great Experiment
great.when: Fri Oct 16 & Sat Oct 17 · 7:15 PM Q&As; daily run continues through Oct 22
great.text: Maing and Metzgar’s political inquiry is most compelling as a conversation starter. Laura Poitras on Friday and Geeta Gandbhir on Saturday give the opening weekend distinct reasons to attend.
great.event: Fri: Stephen Maing, moderator Laura Poitras. Sat: Maing & Farihah Zaman, moderator Geeta Gandbhir.

million.title: One in a Million
million.when: Wed Oct 21 & Thu Oct 22 · 10:50 AM, 1:00 & 7:00 PM
million.text: A decade-long portrait follows Israa from escape to a life in Germany, giving time and adolescence room to complicate the refugee narrative. Both evening Q&As are officially sold out; matinees remain the ordinary screening alternative, with no confirmed rush or waitlist policy.
million.event: Both 7 PM shows: Azzam, MacInnes & Israa; Wed moderator Julie Goldman; Thu moderator not announced.

fjord.title: Fjord
fjord.when: Oct 16–19 · 10:45 AM daily; Tue Oct 20 · 3:50 PM; Wed Oct 21 · 12:45 PM; Thu Oct 22 · 10:45 AM; additional daily sessions on official page
fjord.text: Mungiu’s moral inquiry is a high-fit current release but no longer a scarce festival engagement. Use a convenient regular showing; the earlier filmmaker appearances have passed.

case.title: Case 137 / Dossier 137
case.text: Moll studies the institutional manufacture of truth through an internal police investigation. It is a worthwhile contemporary counterpoint to the week’s American journalism classics, without an event premium.

hell.title: Hellraiser
hell.text: Barker’s erotic body horror belongs in the lineage of formally and sexually transgressive cinema you value. The restoration is the specific reason to revisit it amid a crowded Halloween calendar.

begotten.title: Begotten
begotten.text: Merhige’s degraded monochrome turns myth into an almost illegible moving-image artifact. It is the harsher midnight alternative to Redline, suited to your interest in radical form rather than conventional genre plotting.

fly.title: The Fly
fly.when: Fri Oct 16 · 9:35 PM; Tue Oct 20, Wed Oct 21 & Thu Oct 22 · 8:15 PM
fly.text: Cronenberg’s fusion of desire, decay and scientific hubris remains foundational body horror. Choose an introduced show for context, or Wednesday for the film alone.
fly.event: Fri intro Su Silver; Tue intro Tori Potenza; Thu intro Rebecca Ritchey.

sweet.title: Sweet Rush / Tatarak
sweet.when: Mon Oct 19 · 8:10 PM; Tue Oct 20 · 3:00 PM; Wed Oct 21 · 4:00 PM
sweet.text: Wajda lets fiction fracture around Krystyna Janda’s account of real bereavement. Its self-conscious construction is a closer personal match than a dutiful retrospective checklist, especially with Paweł Szajda present Monday.
sweet.event: Mon post-film conversation with Paweł Szajda

ashes.title: Ashes and Diamonds / Popiół i diament
ashes.text: Wajda’s combustible image-making turns the end of war into a crisis of identity rather than a clean liberation. The centenary series provides the right context for this foundational Polish modernist work.

illiac.title: The Illiac Passion
illiac.text: Markopoulos transforms Prometheus through New York’s underground artists and an intensely personal montage language. The rare print deserves more weight than an easily repeated canonical revival.

exile.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part II — Exile · Chapters 4–5
exile.venue: NYC MUBI GO partners; Film Forum public run
exile.when: GO week Oct 16–22. Film Forum: Fri–Sun 4:00 PM; Tue Oct 20 & Thu Oct 22 · 4:00 & 7:20 PM
exile.text: The live U.S. GO offer names Chapters 4–5, not the entire six-hour Part II and not Chapters 1–3. Worth using for Loktev’s immersive account of exile if you are prepared for the second half; confirm the eligible NYC venue/session in the app rather than assuming every public Film Forum show accepts GO.

possible.title: Possible Love / 가능한 사랑
possible.when: Opens Fri Oct 23 · 1:00, 4:15 & 7:45 PM daily through Oct 28 currently posted
possible.text: Your NYFF Q&A is already completed, so treat this ordinary run as a relaxed revisit. The Paris Theater’s Nov 24 closing pairing on 35mm with Heartbeat is the scarcer event; its time and live inventory are not public in the series page.

hamaguchi.title: All of a Sudden / Soudain
hamaguchi.when: MoMA Thu Nov 19 · 6:00 PM; FLC Nov 18–19 times TBA; opens Nov 25
hamaguchi.text: This is the rewatch to plan around after your strong NYFF response. MoMA confirms Hamaguchi in conversation and exact sale dates; FLC separately announces Hamaguchi and Tao Okamoto for previews but has not published times or sale details.
hamaguchi.event: MoMA Explore+ Nov 5; public Nov 12 · both 10:30 AM ET. Set a personal reminder.

dragon.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn / 不散
dragon.text: The movie-palace elegy remains a direct-focus theatrical priority if you missed recent screenings. No guest is announced, so book for the film rather than an imagined appearance.

ozu.title: The Flavor of Green Tea over Rice / お茶漬の味
ozu.text: Ozu’s careful comedy of marriage and class belongs near the top of your repertory watch. The 35mm screening is a stronger reason to book than an ordinary digital return.

father.title: Fatherland
father.when: Opens Oct 23; Q&As Fri Oct 23 · 6:30 PM & Sat Oct 24 · 4:30 PM
father.text: The new regular run brings another chance at Pawlikowski in person. Given your earlier NYFF Q&A plan, this is an optional second conversation rather than a presumed missing ticket.

closure.title: Closure
closure.when: Opens Wed Oct 28; Q&As Oct 28 & 29 · 6:45 PM
closure.text: A father’s search on the Vistula becomes an immersive study of hope and suspended grief. Both director nights are announced and ticket-linked, making them the useful opening-week choices.

road.title: On the Road
road.when: Preview Sun Oct 25 · 6:45 PM; opens Wed Oct 28 · regular times TBA
road.text: A drifter and truck driver find intimacy in an aggressively masculine landscape. Choose the filmmaker preview for the event upgrade; do not mistake it for the start of the regular engagement.

gentle.title: Gentle Monster
gentle.text: Léa Seydoux leads a domestic drama in which suspicion dismantles the possibility of a fresh start. It is a considered international release to watch, with no guest or showtime announced yet.

birds.title: Birds of War
birds.when: Opens Wed Nov 4 · 6:30 PM Q&A; more times TBA
birds.text: Thirteen years of archives link reporting, revolution, exile and an unexpected relationship. The subjects are also the filmmakers, making opening night a particularly substantive conversation.
birds.event: Q&A with Janay Boulos & Abd Alkader Habak

soul.title: Soul Patrol
soul.text: Harper reconstructs the first Black special-operations team in Vietnam through personal archives and a reunion. It is a promising documentary opening; no new guest-bearing show has been announced on the engagement page.

lantern.title: Raise the Red Lantern / 大红灯笼高高挂
lantern.text: Gong Li’s performance and Zhang’s enclosure of bodies inside ritual are essential Fifth Generation cinema. The new 35th-anniversary engagement warrants a deliberate big-screen revisit rather than a buried calendar mention.

every.title: Everytime
every.text: Wollner’s unsettling family drama returns after NYFF. Either event or regular format fits your prior plan, so this announced run lowers the need to chase a festival-style premium.

bitter.title: Bitter Christmas
bitter.text: Almodóvar’s new film is a notable international opening inside the 30-day window. A regular theatrical release makes it less urgent than rare prints or direct-focus appearances.

making.title: Making Marie Antoinette
making.when: Tue Oct 20 · 6:30 PM; theatrical release Oct 23
making.text: Eleanor Coppola’s long-unseen footage observes Sofia directing at Versailles, turning a production record into a mother–daughter encounter. The free preview is at capacity; MoMI explicitly allows limited standby, so do not assume an RSVP is still obtainable.
